summary.headline: Rushil Decor FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 801 million (9.3% margin) after Q1 fire disruption; Q4 margin recovered to 12.4%.
summary.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: a fire at the Andhra Pradesh MDF facility disrupted Q1 production, and resin/raw material inflation, export logistics issues and Middle East shipping disruption weighed on the year. Consolidated FY26 revenue from operations was INR 8,622 million with EBITDA of INR 801 million (9.3%) and PAT of INR 64 million. Q4 FY26 showed sequential recovery, with revenue of INR 2,309 million (up 6.6% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 286 million (12.4% margin). Management implemented MDF price increases of 15% and Laminate price increases of 10% effective 1 April 2026, mainly to recover cost inflation.

financial_highlights.value: INR 159 million (6.9% margin) / INR 101 million (4.4% margin)

financial_highlights.change: Decline attributed to Q1 production loss and lower MDF exports

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,544 million; net debt to equity 0.39

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 6,091 million and EBITDA INR 601 million (9.9%). Q4 revenue INR 1,668 million, EBITDA INR 233 million (14% margin); India MDF revenue up 37.3% YoY in Q4 and 12.5% for FY26; blended realisation up 9.7% YoY in Q4. Capacity utilisation 83% in Q4, 75% for FY26.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 2,111 million (+6.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 182 million (8.6%). Q4 revenue INR 534 million, EBITDA INR 41 million (7.7%). Domestic revenue +21% YoY for FY26; blended realisation +7.5%, export realisation +13.7%. Utilisation above 91% in Q4 and above 89% for FY26.

segments.name: Jumbo Laminates
segments.commentary: Both phases now operational with 28 lakh sheets per annum capacity (per analyst). Products sold to Russia, Portugal, Slovakia, Romania, Israel, Kosovo and others; brands VIR KLADS, VIR TOPAZ, VIR VAULT. Customer onboarding is long due to certification requirements. Management expects FY27 utilisation of 60-65%, rising to 85% in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give numeric FY27/FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance; four stated priorities: value-added products to 50% of MDF volumes and 60% of MDF revenue (FY26: 42% volume, 54% value), scaling Jumbo Laminates, raising utilisation to about 90% across the year, and aggressive cost optimisation.
Q1 FY27 capacity utilisation expected to be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels (about 83% MDF, above 91% Laminates).
MDF EBITDA margin currently about 8%; target of 10-12% for MDF, driven by value-added mix.
Laminate business EBITDA target of 10-12% on average, with wide range across Jumbo SKUs.
No new debt planned in FY27; scheduled repayment of around INR 50 crores in FY27.

Management estimated Jumbo Laminate potential revenue at 28 lakh sheets x 85% x INR 4,000 per sheet (about INR 950 crores at full utilisation, as per the analyst's arithmetic); management did not confirm the INR 900 crore figure and said it depends on product mix.
capex_capacity: Jumbo Laminate: both phases operational; one facility underwent a major machinery upgrade in April 2026, production ramping up.
Jumbo thickness range 2.1 mm to 18-19 mm versus 0.6 mm to 1.9 mm for conventional laminates; management cited average realisation around INR 4,000 per sheet.
MDF utilisation 83% in Q4 FY26, 75% for FY26; target 90% across the year in FY27.
Laminate utilisation above 91% in Q4 FY26 and above 89% for FY26.
Product mix (approx.): MDF 75%, Laminates 20%, WPC 5%; Jumbo expected to raise laminate share over time.
Management expects three new MDF plants industry-wide this financial year, implying oversupply pressure.
demand_pricing: MDF price hike of 15% and Laminate price hike of 10% from 1 April 2026; management said the hike only offsets cost, with no incremental margin intended.
Chemical prices up roughly 40% since the Middle East conflict began; net impact about 10% of selling price, or about 11% total cost increase per management.
Industry MDF demand CAGR cited at 15-18%; management assumes 650-800 cubic metres per year of new capacity can be absorbed, but sees oversupply near term.

Export: company is not exposed to the US tariffs; laminates are the bulk of exports (Europe, Russia, Western Europe, Baltics, CALA). MDF exports were lower due to Middle East dependence and a calibrated export approach.
Distribution network: 67 new direct distributors and more than 131 retailers and dealers added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What will capacity utilisation look like in Q1 FY27 across plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 would be in the range of Q4 FY26 levels; MDF exports are under pressure, so domestic sales are being pushed, and a Jumbo facility machinery upgrade completed in April is ramping up.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue or EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric guidance; management instead listed four priorities: 50% value-added share, scaling Jumbo, 90% utilisation and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current net debt and FY27-28 debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt (after cash) went from INR 262 crore (Mar 2025) to INR 254 crore (Mar 2026), including about INR 9 crore euro FX impact; about INR 50 crore scheduled repayment in FY27 and no new debt planned.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo Laminate realisation and potential revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realisation around INR 4,000 per sheet on average, with utilisation up to 85%; the analyst's 28 lakh sheets x 85% x INR 4,000 math was confirmed as correct, though management later said the calculation overstates output because higher thicknesses yield fewer sheets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MDF price hike purely cost recovery or margin-accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Purely cost recovery: chemical costs up about 40%, net about 10% of selling price, so total cost up about 11%; no additional margin is being earned.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state MDF realisation and EBITDA margin for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Current MDF EBITDA margin about 8%; target 10-12% through higher value-added mix; value-added share missed target slightly in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Jumbo volume, revenue and margin targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation targeted at 60-65% in FY27 and up to 85% in FY28; Laminate-business EBITDA target 10-12% on average, with wide margin range by SKU.

qa_highlights.question: Industry demand-supply and MDF capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Three new plants expected this financial year, implying oversupply; management was not aware of unorganised-sector capacity closures.

risks_watch: Oversupply from three new industry MDF plants in FY27 could pressure pricing and utilisation despite the 15% MDF price hike.
Raw material risk: chemical/resin costs up about 40% since the Middle East conflict; formaldehyde supplier and pricing details were not disclosed.
Export exposure to Middle East shipping disruption; MDF export volumes remain subdued.
Jumbo Laminates ramp is slow: long certification cycles; FY27 utilisation target of 60-65% is well below the 85% long-term assumption.
Euro FX exposure contributed about INR 9 crore to net debt increase; FY27 scheduled repayment about INR 50 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operational recovery and Jumbo ramp-up, but cautious and non-numeric on FY27/FY28 financial guidance, declining to quantify revenue or EBITDA outcomes. Some answers were evasive, e.g. on formaldehyde suppliers ("can provide later") and unorganised-sector capacity closures ("not aware").

adds.what: Jumbo Laminate second phase / both phases operational (28 lakh sheets p.a. per analyst, not company-confirmed); one facility machinery upgrade April 2026

growth.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance but set margin targets (MDF and laminates 10-12% EBITDA), 90% utilisation, 50% MDF volume from value-added products, and Jumbo utilisation of 60-65% in FY27 rising to 85% in FY28, backed mainly by price hikes (MDF +15%, laminates +10%) and mix, with no new capacity of its own confirmed.
